cards.front: Class II cabinet airflow and clean-to-dirty layout
cards.back: The critical zone is ISO 5 (Class 100), with typical vertical HEPA airflow 0.45 m/s ±20%. Keep grilles and the front opening clear, do not overcrowd or stack, and arrange clean supplies → target culture → waste. A UV lamp does not replace chemical wiping, and a burner must not be used.

Work with one cell line; use a fresh sterile pipette for each vessel or sample; hold closures above the opening or upright, never face down; approach from the side; move slowly and gently; do not talk over exposed product; sanitize gloves before opening and after dirty material.
Incubate for at least 14 total days within 20–35 °C. When two temperatures are used, hold at least 7 days at 20–25 °C first, then at least 7 days at 30–35 °C.

cards.front: Mycoplasma detection and the limit of antibiotics
cards.back: Mycoplasmas are about 0.15–0.3 µm, can pass 0.22 µm filters and can grow without turbidity; 0.1 µm filtration and routine dedicated testing are needed. Penicillin-streptomycin may mask visible growth but does not sterilize the culture.

cards.front: Improved-Neubauer large-square volume and the concentration formula
cards.back: 1 mm × 1 mm × 0.1 mm = 0.1 µL = 10⁻⁴ mL, so viable cells/mL = mean unstained count per large square × 10,000 × dilution factor. Check the depth marked on your own chamber.

cards.front: Boundary rule, corners and the order of decisions
cards.back: Include cells touching the top or left line; exclude any cell touching the bottom or right line, even at a corner. Decide the boundary first, then the stain; excluded cells enter neither tally.

cards.front: Poisson counting uncertainty and what it leaves out
cards.back: About 100/√N percent for N cells counted: 100 cells give 10%, 400 give 5%. It excludes mixing, dilution, loading and classification errors, which replicate agreement cannot reveal.

cards.front: What trypan-blue viability does and does not show
cards.back: The fraction of counted cells with intact membranes at the moment of counting, read in serum-free solution within minutes. Not growth, function, phenotype, sterility or overall health.

cards.front: Nutrients, pH, osmolality, bicarbonate/CO₂ and phenol red
cards.back: Basal medium supplies formulation-specific salts and nutrients. pH and osmolality are different QC quantities. Bicarbonate buffering requires its specified CO₂ environment; phenol red indicates pH shifts but is not the buffer and shows neither osmolality nor sterility. Serum-free is not automatically fully defined.
V_stock = C_target × V_final/C_stock; then V_basal = V_final − ΣV_supplements. For 500 mL at 10% serum plus 1× glutamine from 100×: 50 mL serum + 5 mL stock + 445 mL basal = 500 mL final.

cards.front: Supplement handling and the filtration evidence boundary
cards.back: Reject expired/unidentified lots; preserve frozen/cold glutamine history and avoid repeated freeze–thaw. Heat-inactivate serum only for an application-specific reason. Use an aseptic 0.22 µm protein-compatible filter and an integrity test; neither clarity nor 0.22 µm filtration excludes mollicutes.

cards.front: Supplemented-medium QC, label, storage and release
cards.back: Record additions, component/filter lots, pH, osmolality and filter integrity. Incubate filtrate controls ≥7 days at 20–25 °C then ≥7 days at 30–35 °C and submit dedicated mycoplasma testing. Link dates/expiry and cell line; account for aliquots; store 2–8 °C dark and quarantine pending QC.

Use growth state, morphology, medium and viability together. This simulation chooses 70–85% confluence for routine adherent passage and a separate 95% refusal/investigation branch. Suspension cultures use density and clumping rather than surface confluence. These are synthetic choices, not cell-line acceptance criteria.

Adherent: inspect → remove medium → calcium/magnesium-free wash → dissociate → observe detachment → neutralize → collect/resuspend → count → seed. Suspension: mix/sample → count → dilute directly or transfer a portion and dilute; no substrate-detachment step.

V_cells per flask = N_target/C_viable. V_fresh = V_final − V_cells. For n identical flasks multiply the per-flask inoculum by n. Example: 500000/(1.21 × 10⁶) = 0.413223 mL; at 12.0 mL final, fresh medium = 11.586777 mL.

cards.front: Split ratio, passage number and PDL
cards.back: A split ratio records a proportional transfer, not a guaranteed viable density. Passage number counts subculture events. PDL increment = log₂(Nf/N0); cumulative PDL = previous cumulative PDL + increment. Neither passage number nor PDL authenticates a cell line.
